correctness.rationale: For arbitrary n>=1, the rank-r fixed-atom star is shattered by the mixed-rank antichain constructed for each label pattern; omitted r-subsets are blocked by their unique deleted-atom subsets, and finite maximal extension preserves inclusion/exclusion. Sperner width bounds any support realized all-positive. For n<=5, a self-contained checker enumerates all maximal antichains as maximal cliques, verifies all maximality conditions, uses the exhaustive trace-splitting equivalence and monotone increasing supports to compute every shattered set, including an empty next level; all 120 atom permutations give eleven classes and 310 six-supports. Full local replay succeeded. Finite findings are never extrapolated to exact dimensions above five.

originality.rationale: Semantic published-finding corpus and local-ledger overlap searches and implication comparisons against directly relevant full arXiv material and primary lattice literature did not find the same VC concept-class invariant or a stronger claim implying the exact B5 support polynomial and eleven orbits. Counting/maximality and static poset-width results are not logically equivalent to supportwise all-label realizability. Full-text inaccessibility of Ignatov and alternate historical terms leave a stated finite residual risk; no global novelty theorem is asserted.
residual_risks: The complete 2023 Ignatov paper could not be inspected; its public abstract is enumeration-focused but hidden connections are possible.
A result under alternative terminology (Sperner-family incidence, maximal-clique shattering) may have escaped indexed searches.
The general exponential lower bound may be known through adjacent-level induced matching folklore; the finite 310-support and eleven-orbit classification is the strongest distinctive component.

value.rationale: For a standard extremal family, the new invariant measures learnability of which lattice elements may occur jointly across maximal families; it differs fundamentally from Sperner width or hypothesis counting. A uniform, nontrivial star/blocker construction gives an exponential-order lower bound for all n. The exact five-atom polynomial, complete six-support orbit classification and first VC dimension exceeding number of underlying atoms supply a natural sharp finite benchmark with a plausible role in subsequent high-dimensional shattering studies. Neither independent certification nor a stronger general formula is claimed.
